steps.name: DESeq2 paired LRT and pairwise contrasts
caveats: The counts are described only as 'gene-level counts from Salmon as delivered' with no statement of whether a length correction (tximport/lengthScaledTPM) was applied and no per-sample quantification files or transcript-length table were provided. Per grounded rule R-0169, fit the model on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and state in the report that a change in isoform usage between conditions could appear as differential expression.
DESeq2 flags a count outlier by Cook's distance and sets p-value/padj to NA in cells with <7 replicates (here, 4 per condition) — report these separately from genes dropped by independent filtering.
steps.context: Paired 3-group design (4 subjects, each with control/treated_a/treated_b). This is the central analysis: the LRT answers 'which genes respond to either treatment' and the pairwise Wald contrasts (all against an explicit reference and each other) answer 'do the two treatments differ'. Counts are gene-level from Salmon with no confirmed length correction (no per-sample quant.sf files or average-transcript-length table provided) — fit on counts as delivered with no length offset, and state this in the output.

steps.description: Filter genes to >=10 counts in at least 4 samples (smallest group size). Fit DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition (subject and condition as explicit factors, control set as the reference level of condition, subject IDs as levels of the blocking factor). Run the likelihood ratio test with full model ~subject+condition against reduced model ~subject to detect any gene responding to either treatment. Additionally extract three named Wald contrasts: condition treated_a vs control, condition treated_b vs control, and condition treated_a vs treated_b. Apply ashr shrinkage to each contrast's log2 fold change (contrasts are between non-reference levels/combinations, so ashr rather than apeglm). Keep DESeq2's default count-outlier flagging (Cook's distance, NA p-values in cells with <7 replicates) and report flagged genes. Inspect the p-value histogram of the LRT and of each Wald test before adjustment.

plan.title: Paired 3-group DE (control vs A vs B) + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Four subjects each contribute a control, treated_a, and treated_b blood sample (12 samples, 12000 genes, raw Salmon gene counts, single batch). The design is paired across three conditions within subject, so DESeq2 is fit with subject as a blocking factor (~subject + condition). A likelihood ratio test (full ~subject+condition vs reduced ~subject) finds every gene that responds to either treatment within a subject; named pairwise Wald contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control, treated_a vs treated_b) with ashr shrinkage then resolve which genes differ, in which direction, and whether the two treatments diverge from each other. QC precedes modeling to confirm subjects cluster together and no batch/outlier structure confounds the paired design. Per-contrast fgsea against Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways pathway sets (all confirmed present for human) turns the ranked gene lists into pathway-level hypotheses. A single report step consolidates diagnostics, gene tables, and enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata. The gene-level count table is stated by the profile to come from Salmon with no confirmation that a length offset was applied (no per-sample quant files or transcript-length table are among the inputs), so the model is fit on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and this caveat is carried into the model_design step and the report per the grounded rule.

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
